packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:28 — deleteCache wipes CalendarCache rows but leaves the Google watch channel (googleChannelId) intact and does not re-fetch, and cache misses in getFreeBusyResult never write back, so the credential stays uncached (every availability check hits the Google API) until an unrelated calendar-change webhook fires.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that cache misses are written back: in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, when `getAvailabilityFromCache` returns no cache, it calls `fetchAvailability(parsedArgs)` and then `setAvailabilityInCache(parsedArgs, data)`, so deleting rows via `deleteCache.handler.ts` would be repopulated on the next availability request. While `deleteCache.handler.ts` indeed only `deleteMany`’s `CalendarCache` rows and does not touch `SelectedCalendar.googleChannelId`, the finding’s key claim that the credential will “stay uncached… until an unrelated webhook fires” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:43 — deleteCache onSuccess never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike the disconnect mutation), and the query uses refetchOnWindowFocus:false, so the stale "Last updated" timestamp and delete action keep showing after a successful delete unless the optional onChanged prop happens to refetch.

adjudication.rationale: In CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx, deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback; it does not invalidate/refetch any TRPC queries (unlike disconnectMutation, which invalidates utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and utils.viewer.apps.integrations). adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` the diff adds `import { CalendarCacheRepository } ...` and directly does `const cacheRepository = new CalendarCacheRepository();` then calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:176 — The cache-status groupBy ignores `expiresAt` and takes `_max` across all keys, so expired or partially stale caches still report a fresh "Last updated" time.

adjudication.rationale: In `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, the Prisma `groupBy` only filters by `credentialId` and computes `_max.updatedAt` across all `CalendarCache` rows for that credential. It does not filter out rows whose `expiresAt` is in the past, so if all cache entries for a credential are expired but still present in the table, the UI will still show a non-null `cacheUpdatedAt` (“Last updated”) based on those expired rows. This directly matches the finding and is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 — Backfilling legacy rows with NOW() makes every existing cache show the migration time as its "Last updated" value, which is misleading.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new non-null `updatedAt` column to `CalendarCache` with `DEFAULT NOW()` in the migration and `@default(now()) @updatedAt` in the Prisma schema. The UI then surfaces this via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` (groupBy `_max.updatedAt`) and shows it as “Last updated” in `CredentialActionsDropdown`. For pre-existing rows, the migration will set `updatedAt` to the migration time, so the displayed “Last updated” will reflect migration/backfill time rather than the true cache refresh time. This is a real, diff-grounded semantic/UX concern, but not a hard functional defect since there was no prior timestamp to preserve.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx:28 — deleteCache has no rate limiting, so a user can repeatedly purge their cache and push availability lookups onto the shared Google API project quota.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `viewer.calendars.deleteCache` authed mutation (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx) whose handler (deleteCache.handler.ts) allows an authenticated user to `deleteMany` `CalendarCache` rows for their credential with no visible throttling/guards. While not a functional correctness defect by itself, it does create a diff-grounded abuse/operational risk: a user could repeatedly clear cache and force subsequent availability queries to miss cache and hit upstream providers more often (increasing shared quota usage). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — Every cache refresh (fired by each Google push-notification webhook and watch/unwatch) now does an extra updateMany that rewrites every SelectedCalendar row for the credential, including all event-type-scoped rows, and the new cache-status UI never reads that updatedAt (it reads CalendarCache.updatedAt), so the write amplification buys nothing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts` after cache refresh. `updateManyByCredentialId` updates all `selectedCalendar` rows matching `{ credentialId }`, which includes event-type-scoped rows. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:29 — connectedCalendars, a frequently fetched query, now adds a serial groupBy on CalendarCache for all credential IDs (non-Google ones too), and constructing CalendarCacheRepository directly skips the calendar-cache feature-flag/mock path, so the query runs even when caching is disabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` the handler now always instantiates the concrete `CalendarCacheRepository` (`new CalendarCacheRepository()`) and unconditionally calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds)`, adding an extra DB `groupBy` on `calendarCache` for all connected credential IDs (no filtering by integration type). That’s a concrete performance/architecture concern and it also bypasses any potential DI/feature-flag path that would otherwise use `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` (the mock explicitly exists for when calendar-cache is disabled), since the handler hard-codes the real repository. However, the finding’s wording about a “serial groupBy” isn’t accurate: the diff shows a single `groupBy` with `where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }`, not one query per credential.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:174 — groupBy max(updatedAt) has no (credentialId, updatedAt) index and no expiresAt filter, so it reads every cached row per credential (expired ones included) through the (credentialId, key) PK instead of doing an index-only lookup.

adjudication.rationale: The new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` implementation does `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ by: ["credentialId"], where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }, _max: { updatedAt: true } })` with no `expiresAt` condition, so the reported `updatedAt` can be derived from rows that are already expired (since `CalendarCache` has an `expiresAt` field in the schema). However, the finding’s claim about missing a specific `(credentialId, updatedAt)` index and necessarily scanning “every cached row” via the `(credentialId, key)` PK cannot be verified from this diff (no indexes/PK definition are shown here), so that part is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:25 — Plain Error thrown for missing/unowned credential surfaces as tRPC INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of TRPCError NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, polluting server error logs and hiding the real cause from the client.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler checks ownership via `prisma.credential.findFirst(...)` and, when missing/unowned, does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In a tRPC mutation, throwing a plain `Error` typically maps to an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500) rather than a meaningful NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN response, so the client gets the wrong status/cause and the server treats it as an internal failure. This is directly evidenced by the `throw new Error(...)` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:29 — Unguarded getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groupBy means any cache-table failure (or code deployed before the updatedAt migration) now fails the entire connectedCalendars query (suspense error boundary) for a purely cosmetic field.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `connectedCalendarsHandler` always instantiate `CalendarCacheRepository` and call `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` (new `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy` on `_max.updatedAt`) with no try/catch/fallback. Any runtime DB error (including a deployment where code runs before the `CalendarCache.updatedAt` migration) would now throw and fail the entire `connectedCalendars` query, even though `cacheUpdatedAt` is an enrichment for UI actions. This is a concrete resilience/rollout concern introduced by the new unguarded query, but not a guaranteed functional defect if migrations are always applied before code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — updateManyByCredentialId(id, {}) is a silent no-op (Prisma skips @updatedAt when update data is empty) yet adds an unguarded DB write after cache writes whose failure aborts webhook/unwatch processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:42 — deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars (unlike the disconnect mutation's onSettled), so the stale cache status persists whenever the optional onChanged prop is not supplied.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls optional `onSuccess?.()`; it does not invalidate any TRPC queries (unlike `disconnectMutation`, which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`). Since `cacheUpdatedAt` is derived from `connectedCalendarsHandler` (it adds `cacheUpdatedAt` from the DB), deleting cache without invalidating/refetching `connectedCalendars` will leave the UI showing stale cache status whenever the caller doesn’t supply `onSuccess`/`onChanged` to trigger a refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 — Backfilling all existing rows with DEFAULT NOW() makes stale legacy cache entries report as freshly updated at migration time.

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds a new NOT NULL `updatedAt` column to `CalendarCache` with `DEFAULT NOW()` (migration.sql) and the Prisma schema sets `updatedAt @default(now()) @updatedAt`. The new UI surfaces this timestamp as “Last updated” via `cacheUpdatedAt` (connectedCalendars.handler.ts → `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` max(updatedAt) → CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx displays it). Therefore, any pre-existing cache rows will have `updatedAt` set to the migration time, making legacy/stale cache entries appear freshly updated in the new cache status feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:17 — cleanup always exits 0, so rate-limit and URL-extraction failure paths report success to any caller.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, `cleanup()` unconditionally ends with `exit 0`. That function is invoked on error conditions such as the rate-limit hit (`cleanup` after printing the rate-limit message) and failure to extract the tunnel URL (`cleanup` after "Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL."). Because it always exits successfully, callers/CI would see a success status even though the script failed to perform its intended work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:30 — Reuse branch reads the URL from /tmp/tmole.log, which may be missing or stale if the running tmole was not started by this script, writing a dead or empty webhook URL.

adjudication.rationale: In scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh, the reuse branch (when `pgrep -f "tmole $TM_PORT"` finds a running process) always derives `TUNNEL_URL` from a fixed `LOG_FILE` (/tmp/tmole.log) via `extract_url_from_log`, without ensuring that the running tmole instance is the one writing that log. If tmole was started elsewhere (or /tmp/tmole.log is stale from a prior run), the script can extract an outdated URL and then proceed to overwrite `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` in the env file with that stale value (it only fails if the extracted URL is empty).

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:41 — Wait loop never checks that tmole is installed or still alive, so a missing binary or early crash just spins for 10s and ends in a generic failure message.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, the script starts `tmole $TM_PORT > "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &` and then enters a `for i in {1..20}` loop that only checks the log file for the URL keyword or a specific rate-limit string. It never verifies that `tmole` exists (`command -v tmole`) nor that the background process (`$TMOLE_PID`) is still running. If `tmole` is missing or crashes immediately, the loop will just sleep for ~10s and then hit the generic `Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL.` path, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:30 — When a "tmole 3000" process exists (pgrep matches any user's process) the script trusts the predictable world-writable /tmp/tmole.log, so a local attacker can plant a URL that gets written as GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL, redirecting Google push notifications (which carry the X-Goog-Channel-Token webhook secret).

adjudication.rationale: The new script hardcodes `LOG_FILE="/tmp/tmole.log"` (world-writable location) and, if `pgrep -f "tmole $TM_PORT"` finds any matching process, it reuses that state and reads the tunnel URL from this log via `extract_url_from_log()` without ensuring the log was produced by the currently-running tmole instance or by the current user. This allows a local attacker to pre-create/modify `/tmp/tmole.log` (and potentially run a matching `tmole 3000` process) so the script extracts an attacker-controlled URL and writes it into `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68 — TUNNEL_URL comes from a greedy `https://.*\.tunnelmole\.net` grep of log output and is interpolated unescaped into the sed replacement/.env line, so sed metacharacters (&, |) or extra log text can corrupt or inject into .env.

adjudication.rationale: In scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh, TUNNEL_URL is extracted via `grep -oE "https://.*\.tunnelmole\.net"` and then interpolated directly into a sed replacement: `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|"`. In sed replacement strings, characters like `&` are special (expand to the matched text) and the chosen delimiter `|` is also special if it appears in the URL, so an unexpected URL/log match can corrupt the resulting .env line. This is a real, diff-grounded correctness issue in the script.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — updateManyByCredentialId(id, {}) passes empty data, which Prisma treats as a no-op (it does not bump @updatedAt), and no test checks that SelectedCalendar.updatedAt actually changes, so a mocked or prismock test would hide that the side effect never happens.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts`. The repository implementation calls `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`, and `data` is passed as an empty object. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — The new updateMany side effect in fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache has no assertion in the CalendarService tests, and nothing covers the case where it throws after the cache was already written, which fails the whole refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:25 — The access-denied path throws a plain Error, which surfaces as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN TRPCError, and no test pins the error contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/platform/atoms/selected-calendars/wrappers/SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:129 — The error-branch actions now also hide the remove action when disableConnectionModification is set, and delete-cache now shows in read-only/delegation mode, which are behavior changes with no test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces `DisconnectIntegration` with `CredentialActionsDropdown` in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx`. The new component computes `canDisconnect = !delegationCredentialId && !disableConnectionModification` and returns `null` when `!canDisconnect && !hasCache`. Previously, the “error” card branch showed the remove action when `!connectedCalendar.delegationCredentialId` regardless of `disableConnectionModification`; now it is also hidden when `disableConnectionModification` is true. Additionally, `hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` means the delete-cache UI will render even when `delegationCredentialId` is set or connection modification is disabled (since it doesn’t require `canDisconnect`). These are behavior changes introduced by the diff, and the finding’s point about lacking tests for these new conditions is specific and diff-grounded.
